text:
caroline: heads up — tail latency spike after yesterday's kernel-choice rollout on prod. p95 for text-gen up ~1.7x. looks correlated with prefill-heavy workloads. trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/abcd

alex: which kernel variant did we flip to? int8 fp16 choices?

caroline: we biased scheduler to prefer `cudnn_kv_fast` for short seqs (<=64) to speed gen. perf on throughput looks good but KV hit-rate dropped and evictions increased. logs show frequent KV warmups.

jin: can you paste scheduler / queue metrics? my money's on microbatch churn causing token_budget fragmentation.

caroline: copying snippet from the dashboard:
```
prefill: avg_batch_size=3.2, hold_window_ms=4, token_budget_target=24
decode: avg_batch_size=1.1, starve_count=142/5m
kv_hit_rate: 0.68
evictions/min: 12
```

ben: 3.2 batches for prefill is tiny — we're forming a lot of small batches which both reduces kernel amortization and thrashes the KV cache. two quick levers: increase prefill hold window to 8ms (let batch form) + prefer kv-friendly kernel when `kv_hit_rate < 0.9`. also consider raising token_budget_target to 32 for these flows.

caroline: ran a local canary with hold_window=8ms + kernel override when kv_hit_rate<0.9 + token_budget=32. p95 dropped from 420ms -> 260ms, kv_hit_rate up to 0.93. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/123

sam: sounds promising. canary on prod 10% tomorrow night? I can route a handful of customers to dedicated hosts with the new heuristics.

caroline: yes. i'll add an AB flag, dashboard widgets for `kv_evictions` and `per_kernel_kv_hit_rate`, and a short checklist for rollback.

jin: add a metric for `prefill_microbatch_rate` too — that'll make the batching behavior visible.

perf-bot: deploy job queued (#5678) — canary toggle ready.

caroline: thanks all :thumbsup: i'll post a follow-up with before/after numbers after the canary.
